what: The QR Code Scanner reads QR codes with your phone or computer camera, or from an image: a screenshot, a photo, or a picture you paste from the clipboard. It works in the browser with no app to install.
It is useful when your camera app does not scan codes, when the code is in a screenshot or email on the same phone, or when you want to see what a code contains before you trust it.

Decoding happens on your device. On phones it uses the back camera, and it can switch on the flashlight where the browser allows it. Links are never opened automatically: you see the full address first.
uses: Read a QR code someone sent you in a chat or email by uploading or pasting the screenshot.
Scan a Wi-Fi code to see the network name and password and copy the password.
See the full web address behind a code on a poster or parcel before you open it.
Read a contact QR code (vCard or MeCard) and save it as a .vcf file for your phone.
Scan with a webcam when your phone is not to hand, or decode an image on your computer.
tutorial: Click "Scan with camera" and allow camera access when the browser asks. On a phone the back camera is used. If you have more than one camera, choose another from the list.
Hold the code in the frame
Keep the QR code inside the white frame, about 15 to 30 cm away, until it is found. The camera stops by itself when the code is read.
In a dark place tap Flashlight. It only appears if your phone and browser allow it.
Click the box to choose an image, drag one onto it, or copy a screenshot and press Ctrl+V (Cmd+V on Mac). Rotated, small and inverted codes are handled.
The type is shown at the top, such as Web link, Wi-Fi network, Contact card, Phone number, Email or Text message, with the details laid out clearly.

For a link, the full address and the site name are shown. Warnings appear for unencrypted links, look-alike letters and other tricks. Only http and https links can be opened, and they open in a new tab.
Click Copy text, or the matching action such as Copy password, Call or Save contact. Your recent scans are listed under Scan history on this device; Clear history removes them.
features: Uses the back camera on phones, with camera switching and flashlight where supported.
Scan codes from uploaded, dropped or pasted screenshots and photos.
Shows the full URL and warns about suspicious links before you open anything.
Recognises Wi-Fi, vCard and MeCard contacts, phone numbers, email, SMS and map locations.
Uses the browser's built-in barcode detector when available, with a reliable built-in decoder as a fallback.
Your last 30 scans are kept in this browser only.
No uploads: images and the camera feed never leave your device.

example.title: Worked example: a café Wi-Fi code
example.text: A café has a QR code on the table. You click Scan with camera, allow access and point your phone at it. Within a second the result shows Wi-Fi network, with Network (SSID) Cafe Guest, Password latte2026, Security WPA and Hidden network No. You tap Copy password, open your Wi-Fi settings, choose Cafe Guest and paste the password. The scan is also saved in Scan history in case you need it again.

tips: Clean the camera lens and avoid strong reflections on glossy codes.
If a code is very small or far away, move closer rather than zooming, so it stays sharp.
For a code on your own screen, take a screenshot and paste it here instead of pointing a camera at it.
Read the site name in a link carefully. A code stuck over the real one on a poster can lead to a fake website.
Camera scanning needs a secure https page, which this site uses.
problems: You may have blocked camera access. Click the camera or lock icon next to the address bar, allow the camera, and try again. Another app using the camera can also block it.
No QR code found in the image
Make sure the whole code, including its corners, is visible and sharp. Crop out other codes, and try a larger or clearer image.
Only some phones and browsers allow websites to control the flashlight, mostly Chrome on Android. Use your phone's own torch instead.
Some codes use an old character set. The scanner tries UTF-8 first and then Western encoding; if it is still wrong, the code was made with an unusual encoding.
